results.caption:
You tell your agent your budget is two million dirhams. The truth is you would spend two point five million for the right property.

You think you are protecting yourself. You are actually asking your agent to solve the wrong problem.

Here is what happens next. I search up to two million because that is what you told me. I find properties that fit the number, but not necessarily your investment goals. Meanwhile the property with the better layout, stronger rental demand and much better exit potential might be sitting at two point two or two point three million. You never see it. Not because I am trying to make you spend more. Because you gave me a limit that was not real.

A good agent needs two numbers from you. The amount you would ideally like to spend. And the absolute maximum you would consider for something genuinely better. Those are not the same number.

If your preferred budget is two million, I focus there. But if I know you could reach two point five million, I can show you what the additional money actually buys. Perhaps nothing worthwhile. In that case, keep the money. But perhaps another two hundred thousand dirhams gives you a larger unit, a better position, or a property with far fewer competitors when you eventually sell.

Be careful with your budget, of course. Just do not hide it from the person you expect to advise you. False information does not create negotiating power. It creates bad recommendations.

If you are considering buying in Dubai, visit stevenleckie.com and book a short strategy call. Bring both numbers, your preferred budget and your absolute limit. We can work out whether spending more improves the investment, or simply makes it more expensive.
